sections.content: You know all three tenses: the *imperfecto* (A2 Unit 21), the *indefinido* (A2 Unit 11) and the *pluscuamperfecto* (B1 Unit 1). A memorable account uses them together: the *imperfecto* creates the remembered world, the *indefinido* reports what changed, and the *pluscuamperfecto* supplies what had happened before that change.

items.spanish: Mientras Sherezade hablaba, el rey escuchaba en silencio; nunca había oído una historia así.
items.english: While Sherezade spoke, the king listened in silence; he had never heard a story like that.

items.spanish: La historia lo conmovió porque mostraba que una decisión pequeña podía cambiar una vida.
items.english: The story moved him because it showed that a small decision could change a life.

items.spanish: Cuando terminó la noche, el rey pidió otra historia y dejó el castigo para después.
items.english: When the night ended, the king asked for another story and left the punishment for later.

items.spanish: Desde entonces, cada relato tenía una enseñanza y los dos la recordaban.
items.english: Since then, every tale had a lesson, and both of them remembered it.

sections.content: When you revise a personal account, check whether every tense makes the time relationship clearer for the reader.

sections.topic: contrasting past tenses in Spanish narratives
